claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response.
The as-cast alloy has poor mechanical integrity and is prone to cracking.
A controlled heat treatment, potentially combined with a minor compositional change, can produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale ductile precipitates in the target alloy.
The desired secondary-phase volume fraction is 2–5%.
Dispersed ductile nanoprecipitates will act as crack arrestors.
The nanoprecipitates will blunt stress concentrations and impede crack propagation.
A low precipitate volume fraction will preserve the phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect.
The proposed precipitates will be thermodynamically compatible with the parent phase.
The intervention will substantially improve compressive strength.
The intervention will improve resistance to crack propagation.
The modified alloy will retain its caloric response within 10% of the unmodified alloy.
The intervention is expected to remain effective during magnetic-field-driven caloric operation.
The intervention is expected to remain effective during pressure-field-driven caloric operation.
The intervention is expected to remain effective near the phase-transformation temperature and under caloric cycling loads.
Heat treatment and minor chemistry changes can be kept within the processing and compositional window supporting the desired transformation.
High-entropy alloys can retain stable phase structures and properties after high-temperature annealing.
Hard Laves-phase particles and solid-solution strengthening can increase compressive strength in a BCC V-Cr-Fe-Ta-W alloy system.
Excessive growth or volume fraction of Laves precipitates can deteriorate compressive performance.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes both heat treatment and compositional adjustment, while the intervention makes the compositional change optional and the controlled experiment varies only heat treatment. The tested intervention therefore does not unambiguously match the proposed intervention.
